title: Beating the blitz: the hot route (and why the Vikings' 73% blitz rate matters tonight)
html:
Why this lesson now: the Film Room mirror (football-brief, branch film-room) was checked this run. It still holds one logged game file (data/games/gmum7mktl1wy3.json, "Eagles at Bears, Week 3", no snaps logged) and no review files. So there's no new miss of yours to fix, and no snap of yours this connects to yet. This lesson builds on Lesson 6 (the blitz) and Lesson 24 (counting blockers) with the offense's answer, because tonight's game is the NFL's blitz-heaviest defense against Josh Allen.

The big idea: when the defense sends more rushers than the offense can block, one rusher is free.The offense can't block him. So it has to throw before he gets there.The quick throw into the space he left is called the hot route (or a "hot read").

Labels A–D match the steps below.

  1. A · Count. Before the snap the QB counts possible rushers and blockers (Lesson 24).Here: 6 rushers. The offense has 5 linemen plus the RB. That's 6 blockers, if everyone blocks the right man.
  2. B · The free rusher. Blitzes are built to fool the count. A linebacker shows late, or a safety creeps down.The RB can pick up only one. The other comes free.
  3. C · The hot route. The blitzer left an empty space. A receiver near it, usually the slot or tight end, cuts short into it, often on a quick slant.QB and receiver both have to see the blitz. When they agree, it's called a "sight adjustment".
  4. D · Throw fast. The ball has to be out in about 2 seconds.If it works, the receiver catches it with nobody behind the blitzer. Short throws can turn into long gains.If it fails, it's a sack or a rushed throw. Sunday, Houston sacked Justin Herbert 8 times. Caleb Williams threw 4 interceptions.
  5. Tonight's matchup (Bills at Vikings, 5:15 p.m. PT, ESPN): Brian Flores's Vikings blitz on 73% of dropbacks, the most in the NFL (Covers).Josh Allen ranks 20th of 31 QBs against the blitz this year (88.2 rating, 3 INTs) (CBS).But he has 16 TDs and 2 INTs in six games against Flores defenses. He beats blitzes by throwing hot, or by running.Buffalo's hot-route targets are thin: Khalil Shakir missed Friday, Josh Palmer is doubtful. Watch TE Dalton Kincaid on quick throws.
  6. Why it matters for bets: quick hot throws are short. They keep a QB's yards down unless one breaks long.That's part of why the board leans "Josh Allen: 250+ yards" → NO tonight.

In your drill: if you see a linebacker or safety walk up to the line late, expect a pass, and expect it fast. Log "P". After the snap, write "H" if the ball came out in about 2 seconds to the spot the blitzer left.

Pre-snap blitz hints: more defenders near the line than the offense has blockers (Lesson 19), and one deep safety or none (Lesson 20).

Real examples to watch: tonight, Bills at Vikings (5:15 p.m. PT, ESPN). On each Allen dropback, count the rushers. When 6 come, see where the ball goes. Rewatch: Houston's 8 sacks of Herbert on Sunday (Will Anderson Jr., Jadeveon Clowney and Sheldon Rankins had 2 each).

Video: search YouTube for "hot route vs blitz explained," "sight adjustment NFL," and "Brian Flores blitz breakdown."

Practice it in Football Camp → (Station 7: Read the snap)

quiz.q: The defense rushes 6 and the offense has 5 linemen plus a running back. If the RB blocks one blitzer and a second one comes, what happens?
quiz.w: Six blockers can handle six rushers only if every assignment is right. A disguised extra rusher comes free.

o: A quick throw into the space a blitzer just left
A long bomb over the top
quiz.w: When a linebacker or safety blitzes, the area he was guarding is empty. A receiver cuts into it, and the QB throws fast.

quiz.q: About how fast does a hot throw have to come out?
quiz.w: The free rusher arrives in roughly 2–2.5 seconds. Late means a sack or a rushed, risky throw.

quiz.q: In your drill, a safety walks up to the line late. What should you log?
o: Pass (P), and expect a quick throw
quiz.w: A late walk-up often means a blitz. Offenses answer blitzes with fast passes.
